group.passage: In Geel, a small town in the Flemish region of northern Belgium, caring for the mentally ill follows a surprising approach. Since the 14th century, Geel has had a tradition of welcoming individuals with mental disorders into foster families, allowing them to live like ordinary people. Legend has it that Saint Dymphna, who had escaped to Geel and was martyred there, inspired this informal yet structured system. This unique care model has now become institutionalized and was included in the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023. In Geel, individuals with mental disorders can live with foster families and participate in their daily activities. These days, around 100 individuals with mental disorders live with volunteer foster families in Geel. These foster families not only provide a warm home environment but also receive the supervision of professional medical institutions, with social workers regularly visiting and assessing the patients’ conditions. Despite the significant success, Geel’s care system still faces several challenges. For example, foster families receive a monthly subsidy of 1,200 euros for each patient they host, which can hardly cover the expenses. Second, the conditions of individuals with mental disorders can be complex and variable, requiring continuous professional medical support. Additionally, as society changes, youngsters may lack interest in becoming foster families. While still not perfect, this Belgian system serves as an ideal model for Taiwan to follow. Currently, certain communities in Taiwan have started promoting “Community Support Homes,” where individuals with mental disorders interact with community residents, with professionals on the side. For now, the greatest obstacle lies in the attitude of the residential neighborhood. Many residents still harbor misconceptions and prejudices against people with mental disorders, which can lead to resistance against such initiatives. Hopefully, public education campaigns aiming at reducing such stigma and increasing awareness about mental health issues could help garner community support and facilitate the successful integration of these homes into more neighborhoods across Taiwan.

questions.stem:
Which of the following set of information is mentioned in the passage?
a. International recognition of a care approach.
b. Government support for the mentally ill.
c. The financial reward for the foster family.
d. Various versions of how the tradition came about.
e. How locals perceive those with mental health issues.
f. Major sponsors for the foster care system.
Which of the following is most likely the writer’s purpose of writing this passage?

options.A: To offer solutions to the heavy burden on the national health insurance.
options.B: To highlight how Taiwan can be a role model for treating people with poor mental health.
options.C: To recommend a practice that embraces the mentally ill in the community.
options.D: To raise public awareness of the importance of regular health examinations.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.A: Areas with more high-income households experience less discrimination.
options.B: Initiatives proposed by the government come with sufficient funding.
options.C: Designated facilities for the mentally ill are more ideal than foster families.
options.D: Efforts are made in Taiwan to accommodate those with mental health issues.

questions.stem: In which of the following blanks can the word “stigma” be placed, as used in the last paragraph?

options.A: “Without the social ______ associated with mental health issues, patients would be capable of living like the rest of the public.”
options.B: “The opening of the community mental health center brought desired ______ for people seeking to reduce their caretaking duties.”
options.C: “The government announced increased ______ for community mental health services to improve facilities and services.”
options.D: “The new community care program provides realistic ______ to help staff offer more effective treatment.”
